title: Two skies, and what the taller one costs a frame
question: If that 29 ms could not be given back, would you still want the taller sky (left/A) over the older one (B)?
context_md:
You said the game feels slow. It does, and this is why.

Last night's worldgen change doubled the sky, which drops the whole landscape 95 rows down the screen. **A is what ships now; B is the sky the world had the day before.** Same seed, same spot, same clear midday.

**Painting A costs about three and a half times what painting B costs** — 29 ms a frame, against a 16.6 ms budget for everything. The simulation is fine: it is actually a third faster than the last time anyone measured it. It is the *drawing* that got expensive, and nothing has ever been counting that.

**I do not think this is the price of the sky, and I am not asking you to give it up.** The cost jumps all at once between sky heights 115 and 120 and then stops climbing — it is flat from there to 190 — and it does not depend on how much sky is actually on screen or how big the window is. That is the shape of a bug, not of a bigger picture costing more to paint, and I am chasing it now.

This card is the fallback: **if I am wrong and it really is inherent, which world do you want?** Answer for the look alone — pretend the numbers are equal — and I will take the cost question from there.

One thing I would ignore: B shows more underground because the ground is higher, not because anything about the caves changed.
